text:
sam: FYI ran the long-context soak on qwen-mqa canals last night, seeing steady RAM growth even with KV paging enabled. not a spike — linear slope over ~2h.

maria: can you paste the run id / config? was this with rope_scale=1.0 or the new adaptive scheduling?

sam: run id: qwen-mqa-long-20250315-22, config: kernel=auto, rope_scale=1.25, mqa=true, kv_paging=true, batcher=continuous, max_seq=48k

ellie: interesting — rope_scale>1 historically caused more frequent slot rebase. could be causing page churn + fragmentation. any kernel fallbacks in logs?

sam: yes fallback to generic attention at ~+37m and again at +89m. attaching perf snippet from that interval:

perf-bot: profiling excerpt:
```
TIME 37m13s: kernel_select -> fallback generic_attention (reason: kernel miss - sequence_len > threshold)
alloc.total  = 12.3G
kv.resident  = 9.8G
kv.paged_out = 1.9G
frag_ratio   = 0.28
page_faults  = 213k
context_len  = 31218
```

perf-bot: later at 89m:
```
TIME 89m02s: kernel_select -> optimized_attn_v2 (fallback recovered)
alloc.total  = 13.1G
kv.resident  = 10.6G
kv.paged_out = 1.9G
frag_ratio   = 0.31
page_faults  = 412k
```

maria: frag_ratio creeping from .28 to .31 while resident is rising suggests reallocation patterns (lots of small frees then allocs) not coalescing. Any evidence of slab fragmentation?

sam: yes slab hist shows many small free blocks around 64-256B and some orphaned pages in the journal. snippet: `slab.free_buckets: 64B: 230k, 128B: 190k, 256B: 62k`

ellie: does kv sweep/gc run periodically? If kernel fallback causes copy-on-write of KV map or moves pages, GC timing could lag and page table stays high.

sam: KV sweep configured to run every 10m. sweep logs show it ran but reclaimed <200MB each run during the growth period.

perf-bot: correlating with batcher metrics: continuous batcher had higher concurrency at +40m (3x baseline) which increased prefix reuse misses.

maria: hypothesis: rope_scale=1.25 increases effective token offsets causing slot indexing to prefer higher pages; kernel fallback path writes temporary shadow entries (not fully merged) -> small allocations -> fragmentation -> reduced reclaim efficiency -> linear resident growth.

ellie: that aligns. mitigation ideas: 1) force kernel pinning to optimized_attn_v2 for this workload, 2) tighten sweep to run more aggressively after kernel fallback, 3) coalesce small frees during sweep.

sam: i can repro faster with a smaller workload if we bump max_seq to 12k and loop a few streams. want me to run with kernel=optimized_attn_v2 pinned?

maria: yes pin it and add more aggressive sweep (interval=2m) and enable slab-coalesce=true. also collect heapprofile at +5m intervals.

sam: running pinned canary now: `./run_canary.sh --model qwen-mqa --kernel optimized_attn_v2 --rope_scale 1.25 --kv-sweep-interval 120s --slab-coalesce true --id canary-1749999999`

deploy-bot: canary started on pool: perf-canaries-3 (3 instances) - id canary-1749999999

perf-bot: initial canary snapshot (t=0): alloc.total=11.8G kv.resident=9.1G frag_ratio=0.27

sam: t+20m: alloc.total=12.0G kv.resident=9.2G frag_ratio=0.27 page_faults=12k — growth flat compared to previous run.

maria: good sign. collect full heap profiles and slab hist after 2h and compare to baseline.

ellie: also add telemetry to kernel_select to log why we fall back and which kernel was chosen; we need a tighter signal for future automated routing.

sam: noted — i'll push a small change to kernel selection logging. patch: `log_kernel_choice(ctx, kernel, reason, seq_len, last_fallback_ms)`

maria: longer-term we should consider making KV shadow writes conditional in fallback path (write-through to preallocated buffers) to avoid small alloc churn. open a GH issue with repro steps and attach canary data.

sam: will do. opening issue now -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/5421 (draft)

ellie: thanks — assigning to eng-runtime and eng-ml for triage. if canary stays stable for 6h we can roll a targeted kernel pin for the affected customer pool. :thumbsup:

sam: will follow up with full attachments (heap profiles, slab hist, sweep logs).
